briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Tops the Nation in Per-Capita Sales as Rescheduling Momentum Builds Nationally
briefs.top: Michigan operators have real wins to point to this week — the state leads the U.S. in per-capita legal weed sales and just crossed $17 billion in lifetime revenue, even as the tax fight and a real-estate shakeout create fresh opportunities for well-capitalized players. Nationally, investor confidence in federal rescheduling is climbing and psychedelics medicine keeps clearing regulatory hurdles, even with a procedural DEA delay this week.

local.text: Michigan crowned #1 in per-capita weed sales — Michigan ranks first nationally among recreational states for 2026 sales adjusted for population, beating New Mexico, Montana and Massachusetts.
State market crosses $17 billion lifetime milestone — Michigan's combined adult-use and medical sales have generated an estimated $2.66 billion in state tax revenue since legalization, per the CRA.

Gubernatorial hopeful courts industry with tax-repeal pledge — GOP candidate John James has won backing from top cannabis executives after promising to cut the state's 24% wholesale tax, opening a real path to relief.

Cannabis real estate fire sale creates expansion runway — at least 50 Michigan cultivation and retail properties are now for sale or lease at steep discounts, a buying opportunity for operators with capital.

Record $2M fine levels the playing field — the CRA revoked 20 grower licenses and tied its largest-ever fine against a mid-Michigan operator for shipping dirt and mulch as flower, signaling tougher enforcement that protects compliant brands.

national.text: Investors grow more bullish on rescheduling odds — a new survey found respondents put 65% odds on federal rescheduling within six months, with 47% more bullish on MSOs than six months ago and none more bearish.

DEA rescheduling hits a pause, not a dead end — a judge stayed the Schedule III proceeding to weigh a new GAO report, but the delay doesn't touch the April order already covering state-licensed medical cannabis.

Compass Pathways nears the psilocybin finish line — the company is targeting Q4 2026 for its COMP360 NDA submission after FDA rolling review and a National Priority Voucher, with a possible H1 2027 launch.
MSO Vireo Growth keeps scaling through M&A — its latest deal for Cannabist assets across five states pushes the operator toward roughly 230 dispensaries nationwide.

Functional mushroom category barrels toward $100B — the global market is projected to grow from $42.3B in 2026 to $96B by 2033, a tailwind for cannabis-adjacent wellness brands diversifying their shelf space.
